transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

For the last few weeks I’ve just been on this intense high, like I’m wired all the time and can’t turn it off, and it’s starting to scare people at work. My manager and a coworker actually convinced me to come get evaluated because my behavior has gotten pretty erratic.
Can you tell me more about this 'intense high' you're experiencing - is it more of an irritable feeling or an extremely happy and optimistic one?

It’s really a mix of both. One minute I feel incredibly supercharged and optimistic, pacing around and telling everyone this project is going to change the industry, but the next I’m highly irritable and snapping at my team over minor delays. I just feel constantly on edge, and any tiny question feels like a personal attack on my work.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or appetite since you started feeling this way, or have they remained relatively normal?

They've both been completely chaotic lately. When I'm on a high, I sleep maybe three hours and wake up wired, but other nights I lie awake with intense dread. My appetite is also all over the place—I'll survive on coffee all day and then mindlessly inhale takeout at night, and my clothes are getting looser.
Can you estimate how long these episodes of feeling 'supercharged' and then irritable last, and do you experience any periods where you feel relatively normal in between?

That intense, supercharged feeling lasted for a few weeks, but this heavy, flat crash has been dragging on for about three months now. I haven't really had any normal periods in between lately. It has just felt like jumping straight from that overwhelming high right into this deep, hopeless low.

Can you clarify if these episodes of intense high and then crash have been recurring over a longer period, or if this is the first time you've experienced such a significant shift in your mood and behavior?

This entire severe cycle of the heavy crash and the intense high has been unfolding over the last three months. While I've had some low moods earlier in my life, I have never experienced an intense, revved-up high or heard voices like this before now.
Have you experienced more than one episode of this intense high followed by a crash in the past, or is this the first time you've had this specific pattern of mood swings?

I’ve had some milder ups and downs in the past where I felt low or a bit revved-up, but nothing like this. This is the first time the mood swings have been this intense and disruptive, and it's definitely the first time I've ever heard voices.
Can you confirm if you've had more than one distinct episode of this intense high followed by a crash, or is what you're describing a single, prolonged episode with fluctuations?

Yes, this has been one single, continuous period of being unwell over the last three months rather than separate episodes. It started with that heavy, hopeless crash about three months ago, which then shifted directly into the intense, supercharged high as the project launch got closer.
To clarify, you've had one prolonged episode with both a high and a crash phase, but no clear separate episodes of mania or depression before this, correct?

That's mostly correct for how severe this is, but I actually have had some milder low moods and revved-up states earlier in my life. This current three-month period is just the first time it's been this extreme, and I've never heard voices or felt so disconnected from reality in those past times.
You mentioned hearing voices, can you tell me more about when this started and what the voices are saying?

It's a deep male voice right behind my left ear that started when I hit that intense high around the project launch. It tells me things like, "You were chosen for this," but if I start to doubt myself, it turns harsh and says, "If you screw this up, everyone will be better off without you." I only hear it when I'm in that highly revved-up state, and never during any of my past low moods.

Have the voices or any other unusual perceptions you've experienced during the high periods ever told you to do something specific, or have they been more about commenting on your thoughts or situation?

No, the voice doesn't really command me to do specific tasks. Instead, it just comments on my situation—telling me that I was "chosen for this" when I'm feeling high, or turning harsh and saying "if you screw this up, everyone will be better off without you" when I start to doubt myself.
Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions or beliefs during these episodes, such as seeing things that aren't there or feeling like you have special powers?

Aside from hearing that deep male voice behind my left ear, I did have some very strong beliefs. I truly felt like I was operating on a completely different level than everyone else and could single-handedly transform the entire company if they just got out of my way.
Have you ever experienced a period where you had these grandiose beliefs or heard voices without the intense high or low mood, or have these symptoms always been closely tied to your mood swings?

No, those beliefs and the voice only ever happen when I'm in that intense, revved-up high state. I've never heard any voices or felt disconnected from reality during normal mood periods or even during my past low moods.

Have you experienced any episodes where the voice or your grandiose beliefs led you to do something that, in hindsight, was clearly irrational or dangerous, and you only realized it after the episode passed?

Looking back now that I’ve crashed into this low mood, I realize how reckless my actions actually were. Believing I was the only one who saw the "big picture," I completely overrode my team's input and made risky, unilateral decisions outside of our protocols. I only fully grasped the gravity of what I was doing after I was escorted out of a steering-committee meeting and pulled from the rollout entirely.
Can you describe any instances where the voice you heard or your grandiose beliefs directly influenced your actions in a way that seemed rational at the time but appears questionable now?

I was convinced I was the only one who saw the "big picture" to single-handedly transform the business, so I overrode my team's input and made risky, unilateral decisions outside of protocol. During meetings, I would insist on these unconventional strategies because I truly felt I was operating on a completely different level than everyone else. It felt entirely rational and urgent at the time, but looking back, I can see why I ended up being escorted from the office in such an agitated state.

Have you experienced any periods where the voice or your grandiose beliefs seemed to fade away or become less prominent, only to return later, or have they been consistently present whenever you're in the high state?

They are consistently present whenever I'm in that high state, but they completely disappear once it fades. I never hear the voice or have those intense beliefs when I'm feeling normal or when I crash into these heavy, low periods.

Can you confirm whether the voices or grandiose beliefs you experience during the high states have ever been so compelling that you acted on them without questioning their reality, even if it led to negative consequences?

Yes, during those high states, I completely believed the voice and my own ideas without ever second-guessing them. Because I felt I was the only one who saw the "big picture," I overrode my team and made risky, unilateral decisions, which ultimately led to HR complaints, being pulled from the project, and being escorted from the office.

Can you confirm if the voice you hear and your grandiose beliefs have ever been so real to you during the high states that you didn't question their reality, even when they led to actions that had negative consequences?

Yes, during those high periods, both the voice and my belief that I was the only one who could save the project felt absolutely real. I didn't question them at all at the time, which is why I overrode my team and made those risky decisions that ultimately led to HR complaints and me being escorted from the office.
Have you ever experienced a period where you had a normal mood, without being high or low, and still heard voices or had grandiose beliefs?

No, I've never heard voices or had those beliefs during a normal mood. They only started and occurred when I was in that highly revved-up, manic state around the project launch. Outside of that intense high, I've never felt disconnected from reality like that.

Can you tell me if the voice you hear or your grandiose beliefs have ever been so intense that you lost touch with reality, making it difficult for you to distinguish what's real and what's not, even when you're not in a high or low mood?

No, I've never lost touch with reality or heard that voice when my mood was normal or even during my low periods. Those experiences only ever happen when I'm in that intense, revved-up high state. Outside of that high, I don't have any trouble knowing what's real.
Can you confirm whether the voices and grandiose beliefs you experience are exclusively tied to your mood swings, or if there have been times when they occurred independently of your mood?

Yes, they are completely tied to my mood. I only ever hear the voice and have those intense beliefs when I'm in that revved-up, intense high state. I've never experienced them when my mood is normal or during my low periods.
Have you ever had a period where the voice or your grandiose beliefs seemed to be a direct response to external stresses or events, rather than just being part of your high mood?

Even though the stress of the project was huge, the voice and those beliefs only ever happen when I'm in that highly energized, manic state. I’ve dealt with plenty of occupational stress and low moods in the past, but I've never experienced anything like that unless my mood was completely revved up. They really only seem to show up when I hit that intense high, rather than just from being stressed out.
Have you ever experienced any visual hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to the voice you've been hearing?

No, I’ve never had any visual hallucinations or seen things that aren't actually there. My experiences have been strictly auditory, specifically that deep male voice I hear speaking right behind my left ear.
Have you ever experienced a period where the voice you hear continues even when you're not in a high or low mood, or does it always stop when your mood returns to normal?

No, the voice always stops completely when my mood returns to normal. I have never heard it when my mood is balanced, or even during my low periods. It seems entirely tied to those times when I am feeling that intense, supercharged high.
Can you clarify if the voice you hear is commenting on your thoughts or actions, or if it's providing a running commentary on your surroundings?

The voice is definitely focused on commenting on my own thoughts and actions rather than what's going on in my surroundings. For instance, when I'm working, it tells me "You were chosen for this," but if I start to doubt myself, it turns harsh and says everyone would be better off if I screw up. It doesn't pay attention to the room or anything else around me.
Have you ever had a period where the voice or your beliefs were so strong that you couldn't distinguish between what's real and what's part of your illness, even when you're not feeling high or low?

No, I've never had that happen when my mood was normal or even when I was low. The voice and those beliefs only occur when I'm in that intense, revved-up high state. Outside of those highs, I don't have any trouble telling what's real.
Can you confirm if the voice and grandiose beliefs you experience are present for the majority of the time when you're not in a high or low mood, or if they only occur during those mood episodes?

They definitely only occur during those high mood episodes. I only experience the voice and those intense beliefs when I am in that revved-up, manic state. I have never heard the voice or felt that way when my mood was stable or during past low periods.

Have you ever experienced a time when the voice you heard or your grandiose beliefs seemed to be a part of your normal thinking, rather than something that only occurred during your high or low moods?

No, they have never been a part of my normal thinking. The voice and those intense beliefs only happen when I am in that highly revved-up, manic state. When I am feeling normal, or even during my low moods, I have never heard the voice or felt disconnected from reality in that way.

Have you ever experienced any periods where the voice or your grandiose beliefs seemed to influence your behavior in a way that led to significant distress or impairment in your social or occupational functioning, outside of the context of your mood episodes?

No, they have never caused any issues or affected my life outside of those high episodes. The voice and those beliefs only occur when I am in that highly revved-up, manic state. When my mood is normal, they disappear completely, so they've never impacted me or caused any distress outside of those times.
Can you confirm if the voice you hear is ever critical or commanding towards you, or if it's primarily supportive and encouraging, even when it turns harsh?

Yes, it definitely becomes critical when my mood shifts. It starts out very supportive, telling me that I was "chosen for this," but as soon as I start to doubt myself, it turns harsh and says things like, "If you screw this up, everyone will be better off without you." It isn't commanding me to do things, but those critical comments feel really heavy.
Have you ever experienced any periods where the voice or your grandiose beliefs seemed to persist even after your mood returned to normal, or did they always resolve once the high or low mood passed?

No, they always resolve completely once that high mood passes. I have never had the voice or those beliefs persist during normal periods, nor have I ever felt disconnected from reality during my past low moods. They only ever happen when I am in that intense, revved-up state.
